div.head: Wi 23[a]
div.ab: Gif man Gedes þeuwne esne in heora gemange tihte, his dryhten hine his ane aþe geclænsie, gif he huslgenga sie;
Gif man gedes þeuwne esne in heora gemange tihte, his dryhten hine his ane aþe geclænsie, gif he huslgenga sie;
Gif man gedes þeuwne esne in heora gemange tihte, his drythen hine his ane aþe geclænsie, gif he huslgenga sie.
Wenn jemand einen Slavenknecht [eines] Gottes[hauses] in ihrer [der Hörigen] Gemeinde anklagt, so reinige diesen sein Herr durch seinen alleinigen Eid, wenn der [Herr] Abendmahlsgänger ist;
If someone accuses a slave-servant of a church in their [the dependants’] community, let his lord clear him by his sole oath, if that [lord] is a communicant;
If anyone brings an accusation against a bond servant of a company in presence of the company, his lord shall clear him by his own oath if he (the lord) is a communicant.

If anyone accuses an unfree servant of a community in their midst, his lord is to clear him with his oath alone, if he is a communicant; if he is not a communicant he is to have in the oath another good oath-helper, or pay for him or deliver him to be flogged.
If a person should bring a charge against an unfree servant of a fellowship(?) in their midst, let his lord clear him by his oath alone, if he [the lord] is a communicant.

note.seg: Wie ich II 85. 757 berichtigte, streiche man die Emendation Godes. Man übersetze: ‘eines Konvents hörigen Knecht in ihrem [der Mönche] Stiftskapitel anklagt’. Das Wort gæd ist in Agsä. Poesie für societas (Grein), fellowship (Toller) belegt; die Schreibung e- für æ fällt in dieser späten Hs. nicht auf (vgl. Wb 57 Sp. 1 n. 7a. b; auch Wif 8 schreibt H g'derian für gæd- ‘vereinen’); und manches Wort der Kentischen Gesetze findet sich nur in Poesie wieder, so rinc, leod. — Servos monachi Romanorum habent; Theodor II 8, 4. Auch mit der Emendation Godes konnte dieser Sinn bestehen: ‘monastic esne’ Stubbs Councils III 236. God kann ja ‘Kirchengut’ bedeuten (Abt 1²), homo Dei heisst ein Hintersass des Klosters Gl 384 Sp. 2 Z. 8 v. u. Dagegen ausgeschlossen ist die Erklärung Heywood’s (Diss. on ranks 368) ‘hörigen Priester’

As I corrected at II 85. 757, the emendation Godes should be deleted. Translate: ‘accuses a convent’s bond-servant in their [the monks’] chapter’. The word gæd is attested in Anglo-Saxon poetry for societas (Grein), fellowship (Toller); the spelling e- for æ is not surprising in this late MS (cf. Wb 57 col. 1 n. 7a. b; at Wif 8 too H writes g'derian for gæd- ‘unite’); and many a word of the Kentish laws recurs only in poetry, e.g. rinc, leod. — Servos monachi Romanorum habent; Theodor II 8, 4. This sense could stand even with the emendation Godes: ‘monastic esne’ Stubbs Councils III 236. For God can mean ‘church property’ (Abt 1²); a dependent tenant of the monastery is called homo Dei, Gl 384 col. 2 l. 8 from bottom. On the other hand Heywood’s explanation (Diss. on ranks 368) ‘bond priest’ is ruled out
Versammlung zu Gottesdienst und Gericht; Toller
Assembly for divine service and for judgement; Toller
Vgl. Gl Eineid 2a; abendmahlsfähige 1. Es kam an auf die kirchliche Frömmigkeit des Schwörenden, dessen Eideswert davon abhing, nicht auf die des verklagten Sklaven
Cf. Gl Eineid 2a; abendmahlsfähige 1. What mattered was the churchly piety of the one swearing, on which the value of his oath depended, not that of the accused slave

All editors emend to Godes. But it is difficult to understand why, if such a scribal mistake had been made, it should not have been corrected. Heora also presents a difficulty. Liebermann understands the expression to refer to a religious community. But is it likely that the head of such a community would not be a communicant? The word gæd occurs in the sense of ‘union,’ ‘association’ (abstract) in Salomo and Saturn, v. 449 (cf. gegada, etc.); and it seems to me not impossible that this may be the same word (with Kentish e for æ) used in a concrete (collective) sense. But I do not feel any confidence in the suggestion.
